sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Supply of Drummed and Bagged Penetration Grade Bitumen

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (RCS of the District of Luxembourg and Luxembourg-City)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1988; applicable for ultimate-source principals)
Luxembourg-Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement (1968, as amended; relevant for Benelux trading counterparties)
Luxembourg-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (2012, as amended; relevant for bitumen refinery sourcing)
Luxembourg-France Double Taxation Agreement (1958, as amended; relevant for logistics and container freight corridors)
Luxembourg-USA Double Taxation Agreement (1996, as amended; relevant for USD-denominated asphalt clearing)
EU/EEA Freedom of Establishment (Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 49 and 54)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme (2004 AML/CFT Law), as amended by the Law of 11 January 2023; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 relative au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE Law), as amended by the Law of 25 July 2020; Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 (SCSp regime, Articles 945-1 to 945-9); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Loi du 31 mai 1999 sur la domiciliation des sociétés; CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 and C-601/20) restricting public RBE access

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized constitutive deed (acte notarié) of the SCSp, in French, German or English with Luxembourg statutory attestations; equivalent to articles of association for non-registered partnerships
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary admitted to the Bar of Luxembourg (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg) performing mandatory AML/KYC verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, articles of association and certificate of good standing (certificat de bonne tenue) of the corporate General Partner and of any corporate founder or ultimate mother-entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the origin state (e.g., Netherlands Chamber of Commerce-KvK, UK Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, RCS Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague_Apostille or Consular Legalization when origin state is not a Hague Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the beneficial-owner register (or equivalent UBO/PSC declaration) for each corporate partner and for each 25%-or-more ultimate shareholder in the chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-state UBO register (e.g., Netherlands UBO Register, UK PSC Register, Germany's Transparenzregister, Delaware BOI reporting as applicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of valid passports (all pages including endorsements) of the SCSp's gérant, natural-person General Partner and all ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the passport-issuing state, with notarial certificate matching the original; apostille where certification is made by a foreign notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from criminal records (certificat de casier judiciaire) or equivalent police clearance certificate of each natural-person manager, issued within the last 90 days
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records authority of the manager's residence (e.g., France Casier Judiciaire, Germany Bundeszentralregister, Netherlands Justis-VOG, FBI for US persons)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration signed by each partner or contributor, confirming the commercial reputation and legitimate origin of the funds to be contributed (no minimum capital is due for the SCSp, but a source-of-funds statement is required by the notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution in the EU/EEA, Switzerland, UK, US or equivalent FATF-compliant jurisdiction; countersigned by the partner/contributor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification (EU/EEA signature recognition); Hague_Apostille for non-EU signatories

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of the General Partner, gérants, legal representatives, shareholders and UBOs against: (a) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and UN Security Council consolidated list (SCR 1267/1989 and SCR 1373); (b) US OFAC SDN list as USD-clearing and SWIFT compliance standard; (c) UK OFSI consolidated list; (d) Luxembourg national asset-freeze measures and CSSF Circular 18/698 PEP guidance. Politically Exposed Persons from foreign states trigger enhanced due diligence (EDD), requiring independent source-of-wealth documentation and senior-management sign-off before the notarial deed. Any sanctions positive hit or unresolved PEP risk produces an automatic Suspicious Transaction Report to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier, CRF) within 24 hours, and the incorporation file is frozen until clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) at www.lbr.lu, the official electronic platform of the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés); name availability is checked via the name-inquiry module and formally reserved by the notary's pre-registration request
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be expressed in any EU official language but must include the statutory suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale' when used in the partnership. Names in non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese, etc.) must be transliterated into Latin characters for RCS indexing; the transliterated version must be identical to the phonetically approved form in the constitutive deed. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public order, identical or confusingly similar to an already registered business name or protected trademark in Luxembourg.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg / Luxemburg / Lux — requires prior authorization of the Minister of the Economy
Banque / Bank / Banking — requires CSSF banking license
Assurance / Réassurance / Insurance — requires CAA insurance license
Fonds / SICAV / SICAR / RAIF / Investment Fund — implies regulated undertaking status requiring CSSF authorisation or registration
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Exchange — requires FSMA-style recognition and may mislead as to regulated venue status
État / Etat / Gouvernement / Ministère / Nationale (in state-implying combinations) — prohibited as false state-affiliation
Société Anonyme / S.A. / S.à r.l. / SCA / SCS / SECA — foreign or incompatible corporate form suffixes not permitted for an SCSp

Names containing bitumen/asphalt descriptors implying certified petroleum quality standards (e.g., 'Premium', 'Certified', 'ISO') without supporting certification, or otherwise misleading commercial labels
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name, the RCS registrar issues a reasoned refusal notice referencing the conflicting register entry or statutory prohibition. The applicant may file a written administrative objection (recours gracieux) with the RCS registrar within 15 days of the refusal notice, providing evidence of consent from the conflicting name-holder or ministerial authorization where relevant, or a revised compliant name. If the administrative objection is denied, judicial appeal lies to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber), to be filed through a Luxembourg avocat within one month of the denial. During the appeal period the proposed name is placed on hold, blocking competing filings. The administrative objection is free of charge; a one-month extension of the initial reservation may be granted upon filing of the appeal with the court and payment of the EUR 10 renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent (société de domiciliation) under the Law of 31 May 1999, as amended. The agent must maintain a physical address in Luxembourg, be staffed during business hours, keep the statutory registers and corporate records, and hold the full AML/KYC identification file of the General Partner and UBOs. A pure mail-forwarding arrangement without a Luxembourg physical service agent is not acceptable for a wholesale bitumen-trading SCSp when tax transparency and substance substance are required for treaty benefits or VAT registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35-45% probability of an unannounced inspection during the first fiscal year: the Grand-Ducal AML implementing framework authorizes random CSSF and RCS verification visits to domiciliation agents whose portfolio includes ISIC 4661 wholesale commodity traders; the Luxembourg VAT and Excise administration (AEDT) may additionally carry out surprise stock-record inspections at the registered office or logistics hub for liquid fuels and petroleum derivatives. Penalties for non-compliance include criminal fines up to EUR 5,000 under Article 1067-12 of the 1915 Company Law and potential withdrawal of the domiciliation authorization.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and preliminary RCS reservation (processed through the Luxembourg notary intermediary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS - Ministère de la Justice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of approximately EUR 10 for the name reservation plus notary handling charge of EUR 30-40; market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing and mandatory publication of the SCSp deed in the RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RCS Luxembourg and the official electronic compendium (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory e-filing fee of approximately EUR 24.50 plus RESA publication fee of approximately EUR 19-40; aggregate EUR 60-90

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the SCSp constitutive deed and AML/KYC certification of the partner and UBO declarations by the Luxembourg notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial scale for a standard SCSp deed with no minimum capital and one corporate General Partner: EUR 1,500-2,000 including disbursements and statutory AML checks

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign constitutive documents, criminal records and passport copies (estimated 3 instruments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent international authentication authority in the document's country of origin (e.g., Apostille Office of the Ministry of Justice, Luxembourg Embassy or Honorary Consulate)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention standard tariff of EUR 30-50 per apostille; consular certification fee of EUR 35-50 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional legal due-diligence memorandum: UBO piercing of the partner chain, source-of-funds review, PEP/sanctions screening report and AML compliance file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm admitted in Luxembourg (Barreau de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hourly benchmark of EUR 250-320; estimated 8-10 hours for a two-tier UBO structure; fixed dossier fee of EUR 2,400-3,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation agreement (first fiscal year prepaid) with physical Luxembourg address, corporate records keeping and regulatory mail handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent (société de domiciliation réglementée)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial tariff of EUR 1,900-2,400 per annum for a non-trustee domiciliation service with corporate-secretarial support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SCSp's UBO details in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), mandatory within one month of inscription
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Ministère de la Justice (electronic filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory zero-filing-fee regime under the Law of 13 January 2019; no public charging fee applies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank business-account onboarding and AML/KYC approval for the SCSp, including PEP/sanctions automated screening and Swift LC/TT payment-rail pre-authorization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank licensed in Luxembourg or EU/EEA
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 300-800 for the initial account package including digital KYC and compliance review; excludes banking fees and transaction charges

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, particularly the provisions on the Special Limited Partnership (Société en Commandite Spéciale) introduced by the Law of 10 August 2016; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the company register; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 January 2010 on the RCS filing formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg, operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Convention de Société en Commandite Spéciale) and the RCS extract of the formation deed (Extrait de l'acte constitutif), lodged electronically via the LBR portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement and no escrow deposit is required for cash contributions to the SCSp.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the first meeting of the General Partner of the SCSp, the undersigned partners unanimously resolve: 1. To accept the initial subscriptions to the partnership interests of the SCSp as set out in the subscription register; each subscriber accepts the partnership agreement and covers the agreed capital contribution. 2. To adopt as the registered office the address evidenced by the landlord’s consent letter and instruct the managers to complete any change notification. 3. To appoint the persons identified in Schedule A as conducting managers (gérants), with sole discretion to represent the SCSp and file all registration and regulatory filings. These resolutions took effect on approval and are recorded in these minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS online name search via Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the preferred SCSp name through the LBR electronic registry system. Verify the absence of conflicting legal entities and obtain availability confirmation. Record the approved name in the draft partnership agreement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing legal entity, alter the name to a distinct phonetic or structural variant and rerun the availability check before signing the agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Signing and notarization of the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary; notarization optional except for real property contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Parties sign the partnership agreement and make their initial capital subscriptions. If contributions consist of real estate, registered vessels or other assets requiring land registry registration, the deed must be notarized. In all other cases the private deed may be executed directly; parties may nevertheless choose notarial certification for evidentiary certainty and to satisfy commercial counterparties.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID of each partner
General partner's corporate documents, if any
RCS excerpt of a corporate general partner
Registered office availability proof, e.g. lease agreement or owner's consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization becomes mandatory or is requested, schedule a notary appointment, re-sign the deed and obtain a notarial instrument; this will not require re-authorization by the partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers online filing portal (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the LBR portal, complete the initial registration application for an SCSp, attach the signed partnership agreement or its certified extract, the list of conducting managers, and the registered office consent. Pay the applicable RCS fee electronically. The RCS reviews the file, verifies the officers' capacity and assigns the Luxembourg registration number.
required_dossiers: Completed RCS initial registration form for an SCSp
Certified copy of the partnership agreement
Statement of acceptance by the general partner
Identity documents of the conducting managers
Payment confirmation of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, respond within fifteen days with additional legalized documents or explanations; correct the registration form and resubmit through the portal without a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and legal effectiveness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Legal Publications Department (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations, RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS transmits the legal extract to the RESA for publication. The publication provides legal publicity and marks the date from which the SCSp's constitutional provisions are opposable to third parties.
required_dossiers: No applicant submission; RCS handles the publication ex officio
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA extract contains typographical or legal errors, file a rectification request with the RCS; the correction will be published without affecting the initial registration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner; RCS for beneficial ownership register; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT/EORI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the partners' register and the manager decision book; file the beneficial ownership declaration with the RCS Register of Beneficial Owners; obtain a LEI code if required by trading counterparties. If cross-border wholesale trading of bitumen is anticipated, apply separately to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT number and EORI number.
required_dossiers: If VAT/EORI sought: identity documents, business plan or first trade contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership declaration is rejected, correct the ownership diagram and refile; if VAT/EORI is delayed, escalate to the AEDT international desk with proof of trading activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie), General Directorate for Industry and Innovation; Administration de l'Environnement for environmental aspects
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operational industrial permit is required for pure containerized wholesale trading of bitumen and asphalt products. A future installation for storage or drumming would require an environmental operating authorization under the Law of 21 June 1976 on classified establishments.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for wholesale trading activities without on-site storage or handling. If a later asphalt/bitumen storage facility exceeds thresholds, a full EIA report would be required under Annex IV of the Law of 21 June 1976 and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 25 May 1976.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at formation. For any future storage operation, compliance thresholds would include: VOC annual fugitive emissions below 10 tonnes per year, odour-abatement controls, oily stormwater pre-treatment and oil-water separation before discharge, and waste handling in accordance with the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for an SCSp engaged exclusively in trading and logistics with no employees and no physical premises. If a warehouse or tanking site is subsequently operated, the operator must obtain a fire safety conformity certificate from the fire department, a structural load inspection certificate from a licensed engineering office, and an occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified filing portal: MyGuichet.lu (eTVA/impotsdirects.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) through a notary or approved e-filing channel to obtain the 11-digit national business number (numéro de matricule). Separately apply to the AEDT via the MyGuichet/eTVA portal for the 15-character Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU followed by 8 digits). Non-resident partners may execute powers of attorney; apostilled constitutional documents and proof of registered office in Luxembourg are required. No Luxembourg minimum capital is required for the SCSp.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg direct tax purposes (no corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at entity level; each partner is taxed on its distributive share as it arises). For VAT, the SCSp acts as an independent taxable person in its own name when carrying out economic activity. No territorial tax-exempt zone applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law; SCSp pass-through treatment is mandatory for direct tax purposes. Where a partner jurisdiction classifies the SCSp differently, anti-hybrid rules under ATAD 1 and ATAD 2 (Luxembourg law of 27 December 2021) and DAC6 disclosure obligations may apply; taxpayers may only align entity classification with foreign treatment to the extent permitted by Luxembourg VAT law and EU anti-hybrid carve-outs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA), harmonized under EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-resident suppliers or for import/export transactions; the EU-wide EUR 10,000 distance-selling threshold applies to cross-border B2C/remote supplies; resident small businesses may qualify for the annual EUR 35,000 turnover exemption from VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Peppol-BIS B2B e-invoicing is being phased in from 1 January 2026 for large taxpayers and 1 January 2027 for all taxpayers; e-invoices must be transmitted via certified Peppol access points and archived for 10 years; VAT returns are filed electronically through the eTVA/MyGuichet portal. Luxembourg currently applies no real-time fiscal clearance, government API pre-clearance, or digital stamping regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of bitumen/asphalt goods physically dispatched or transported by the seller or for the seller's account from Luxembourg to destinations outside the EU are zero-rated under Article 40 of the Luxembourg VAT law (implementing Article 146 of the VAT Directive), provided the goods leave EU customs territory intact within 90 days of supply and the exporter retains conclusive documentary proof of export. Intra-EU B2B supplies remain taxable at destination via reverse charge or are intra-EU exempt only with the customer's valid EU VAT number.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document SAD/DAU) submitted via the PLDA customs portal
Bill of Lading for containerized sea freight (or CMR/airway bill as applicable)
Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or equivalent bank FX confirmation evidencing repatriation of export sale proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration may audit export evidence within the standard VAT assessment period of three years, extended to five years for irregularities or intentional evasion. Missing, incomplete, or false proof of export triggers reassessment of output VAT at 17%, monthly late interest of 0.6%, administrative fines of up to EUR 15,000 per enforceable claim, clawback of previously credited input VAT on related purchases, and criminal sanctions for willful VAT fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); the national central bank of Luxembourg and constituent of the Eurosystem. Foreign-exchange, payment-system, and prudential banking supervision is exercised jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), while economic and financial sanctions are implemented by the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the CSSF.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible, and Luxembourg applies no exchange-control statute. Current-account and capital-account operations are liberalised under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, subject only to EU and UN sanctions screening by correspondent banks. The SCSp is a transparent special limited partnership; profit distribution to partners is governed by the limited partnership agreement (LPA) and Luxembourg insolvency rules, not by currency restrictions. No authorisation, registration, or declaration is required for remittance of profits, return of capital, or repayment of partner loans.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline applies to export proceeds in Luxembourg. Foreign-currency receipts from wholesale bitumen sales (commonly USD or EUR) may be retained in an onshore foreign-currency account, converted at market rates, or applied directly to offshore trade payables at the entity's discretion. The only operative controls are the EU Wire Transfer Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 information requirements and EU/OFAC sanctions checks applied by clearing banks.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Multi-currency Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Commodity Trade Finance Account
Operational Account with Trade Finance and LC Lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an ancillary payment house; Low as a primary clearing rail. An EEA-authorized electronic money institution (EMI) with a PSD2 passport may lawfully hold funds and execute payments for a Luxembourg SCSp under the Luxembourg Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, as amended by the Law of 3 July 2020, subject to safeguarding rules. Offshore EMIs (UK, Swiss, Hong Kong, Singapore) cannot passport into Luxembourg and would require a full CSSF branch licence. In practice, EMIs do not provide correspondent USD clearing for commodity trades, will not hold capital escrow, and frequently exclude wholesale petroleum-product traders; their use should be limited to small operating disbursements and employee expense payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the standard expectation of Luxembourg clearing banks. The General Partner (associé gérant commandité) and each natural-person beneficial owner above 25% must be identified. Remote video identification is permitted only under CSSF Circular 20/718, which mandates a certified video tool, liveness detection, and a compliant audit trail; acceptance is discretionary and limited to standard-risk profiles. For an SCSp active in commodity trading, tier-one banks require at least one face-to-face interview in Luxembourg (or at an embassy or notary for offshore principals) before activating unrestricted operational and trade-finance functions. A remotely opened account is feasible only in a restricted escrow configuration with no outgoing wires until physical or certified KYC finalisation. Where LPA governing law or UBO residence is outside the EEA, apostilled or consular-certified corporate and passport documents are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity-trading classification: bitumen is mapped to petroleum-product trading, which activates enhanced due diligence (EDD) and trade-finance scrutiny of warehousing, transport, inspection, and end-use.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transactional trail per shipment: signed sale and purchase agreements, invoices, Incoterms declarations, bills of lading and container waybills, SGS or equal quality certificates for penetration-grade bitumen, marine and cargo insurance policies, and payment instructions aligned to LC terms, enabling the bank and its correspondent to perform end-to-end reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp pass-through establishment: banks treat the SCSp as a potential nominee or asset-holding vehicle because it lacks a board of directors and management is vested solely in the General Partner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current RCS extract, executed LPA demonstrating genuine economic sharing, the CSSF-compliant UBO declaration and, if applicable, the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) filing, audited or reviewed accounts of the General Partner, and an independent legal opinion confirming that the General Partner exercises discretionary management and that no hidden nominee relationship exists for any UBO above 25%.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March of the following calendar year; confirmation must be submitted once per year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 12,500 per violation; repeated or deliberate non-compliance may result in criminal penalties of up to EUR 1 million and/or imprisonment; failure to maintain accurate UBO data may lead to administrative sanction orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, filing is due by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the legal deadline triggers a formal notice from the RCSL and possible court-ordered coercive fine (astreinte) of up to EUR 250 per day; continued non-compliance can lead to judicial dissolution and strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Declaration (Déclaration fiscale annuelle) for the SCSp as a fiscally transparent partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes, ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May following the tax year; extensions to 30 June or 31 December may be granted upon reasoned request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of up to 10% of assessed taxes; interest on unpaid taxes accrues at 0.8% per month; intentional non-filing or fraudulent filing may be subject to administrative fines and criminal prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit (réviseur d'entreprises) required if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three criteria on a year-end basis: balance sheet total above EUR 6,000,000; net turnover above EUR 12,000,000; average number of employees above 50. Audit is also compulsory if the SCSp qualifies as a public-interest entity or issues securities to the public.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP (law of 19 December 2002 on trade and companies registers and annual accounts, transposing EU Accounting Directives); consolidated financial statements may apply IFRS as adopted by the European Union.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file an annual confirmation with the RBE attesting that the beneficial owner information on the register is accurate and up to date. All changes affecting the beneficial owner, including shareholding transfers that alter beneficial ownership, must be filed with the RBE within one month of the change. Failure to provide truthful confirmation constitutes an infringement subject to administrative fines and, in severe cases, criminal sanctions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners (Registre des Commandités)
Minute Book containing Resolutions of Partners and Management Decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,500 - $16,500 per year for a certified independent audit (réviseur d'entreprises)
